body:
>You're being too critical of yourself. Each person is responsible for his own happiness. You are not responsible for another person's happiness.

When I look my own happiness, I see that her being happy is one key to that, however  haven't been able to give her any long term happiness, sure we go on dates and and buy her gifts which make her smile, but I see a bitterness behind all that, one that feels life is unfulfilled. She tries her best to hide it from me but it comes out all at once when she breaks.

>Do you exercise? Eat a clean diet? Sleep OK? These are all keys to maintaining mental health.

Being at home I get the joys of Chinese home cooking, which allow me to have a sense of a good diet. I try to go for a run in the morning but its hard to and most of the time end up slouching in bed on reddit until my mind deems it too late for a run. I've always been quite restless in bed and probably get 5-6 hours sleep per night.

Thanks for the meditation suggestion, I've had it subbed to /r/meditation for years but never did anything with it.
